solution:
The transpose is obtained by writing the rows of \(A\) as columns. The first row \((1, 3)\) becomes the first column and the second row \((-4, 5)\) becomes the second column.

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -4 \\ 3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(A\) is of order \(2 \times 3\), so \(A^{T}\) is of order \(3 \times 2\). Write the rows \((2, -6, 1)\) and \((-4, 0, 5)\) of \(A\) as the two columns of \(A^{T}\).

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ -6 & 0 \\ 1 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\)
_note: Book's printed answer for Q1(ii) gives the \((2,1)\) entry as \(6\); it must be \(-6\), since the \((1,2)\) entry of \(A\) is \(-6\). A dropped minus sign in the answer key (the neighbouring \(-4\) prints its minus normally on the same page). Our answer is correct.

solution:
Let \(A = \left[ a_{ij} \right]_{3 \times 3}\) with \(a_{ij} = 2(i - j)\). Then \(a_{11} = a_{22} = a_{33} = 0\), \(a_{12} = 2(1-2) = -2\), \(a_{13} = 2(1-3) = -4\), \(a_{21} = 2\), \(a_{23} = -2\), \(a_{31} = 4\), \(a_{32} = 2\).

\(A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 4 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 4 \\ -2 & 0 & 2 \\ -4 & -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

Here \(a_{ji} = 2(j - i) = -a_{ij}\), that is \(A^{T} = -A\), so \(A\) is skew symmetric. Also \(\left( A^{T} \right)^{T} = A = -A^{T}\), so \(A^{T}\) is skew symmetric as well.

Both \(A\) and \(A^{T}\) are skew symmetric matrices.

\(2A = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & -6 \\ 8 & -6 \\ -4 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), so \((2A)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & 8 & -4 \\ -6 & -6 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).

Also \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 & -2 \\ -3 & -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(2A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & 8 & -4 \\ -6 & -6 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\).

The two matrices have the same order and equal corresponding entries.

\(\therefore (2A)^{T} = 2A^{T}\)

\(3A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 & -15 \\ 6 & -9 & 12 \\ -15 & 12 & 27 \end{bmatrix}\), so \((3A)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 & -15 \\ 6 & -9 & 12 \\ -15 & 12 & 27 \end{bmatrix}\).

Also \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -5 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \\ -5 & 4 & 9 \end{bmatrix}\) (here \(A\) happens to be symmetric), so \(3A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 6 & -15 \\ 6 & -9 & 12 \\ -15 & 12 & 27 \end{bmatrix}\).

Corresponding entries are equal.

\(\therefore (3A)^{T} = 3A^{T}\)

Writing the rows of \(A\) as columns,

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1-2i & 2-i \\ 1+2i & 0 & 7 \\ i-2 & -7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

Multiplying every entry of \(A\) by \(-1\),

\(-A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -(1+2i) & -(i-2) \\ 1+2i & 0 & 7 \\ -(2-i) & -7 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1-2i & 2-i \\ 1+2i & 0 & 7 \\ i-2 & -7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

since \(-(i-2) = 2-i\) and \(-(2-i) = i-2\). All corresponding entries agree.

\(\therefore A^{T} = -A\), i.e. \(A\) is skew symmetric.

\(A + B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 9 & -5 \\ -9 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\), so \((A + B)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -9 \\ -2 & -5 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\).

Also \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & -6 \\ -3 & -4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 4 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(A^{T} + B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 & -9 \\ -2 & -5 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(\therefore (A + B)^{T} = A^{T} + B^{T}\)
_note: The stem as printed reads \((A + B) = A^{T} + B^{T}\), with no transpose on the left-hand side; as printed the two sides are of orders \(3 \times 2\) and \(2 \times 3\), so the statement is meaningless. Solved as the intended \((A + B)^{T} = A^{T} + B^{T}\), which is also the form of sub-item (ii).

solution:
\(A - C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ 6 & -8 \\ -4 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\), so \((A - C)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 6 & -4 \\ -5 & -8 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\).

Also \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & -6 \\ -3 & -4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(C^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & -2 \\ 2 & 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(A^{T} - C^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 6 & -4 \\ -5 & -8 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(\therefore (A - C)^{T} = A^{T} - C^{T}\)

From \(3A - 2B + C = I\) we get \(C = I - 3A + 2B\).

\(3A = \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 12 \\ -6 & 9 \end{bmatrix}\), \(2B = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 6 \\ 8 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 12 \\ -6 & 9 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 6 \\ 8 & -2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -16 & -6 \\ 14 & -10 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(C^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -16 & 14 \\ -6 & -10 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(4B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 8 \\ -8 & 4 \\ 12 & -16 \end{bmatrix}\).

Adding corresponding entries,

\(A^{T} + 4B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 8 \\ -5 & 8 \\ 12 & -18 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(5A^{T} - 5B^{T} = 5\left( A^{T} - B^{T} \right)\), and

\(A^{T} - B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 0 \\ 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \\ 3 & -4 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 7 & -2 \\ 5 & 3 \\ -3 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(5A^{T} - 5B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 35 & -10 \\ 25 & 15 \\ -15 & 10 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(2B = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & -8 \\ 6 & 10 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(3C = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 6 & 9 \\ -3 & -3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(A + 2B + 3C = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 8 & 2 \\ 6 & 8 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\), giving \((A + 2B + 3C)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 8 & 8 \\ 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\).

For the right-hand side, \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), \(2B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 2 & 10 \\ -8 & -4 \end{bmatrix}\), \(3C^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -3 \\ 6 & -3 \\ 9 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(A^{T} + 2B^{T} + 3C^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 6 \\ 8 & 8 \\ 2 & -2 \end{bmatrix}\)

Both sides are equal.

\(\therefore (A + 2B + 3C)^{T} = A^{T} + 2B^{T} + 3C^{T}\)
_note: The stem as printed reads \((A + 2B + 2C)^{T} = A^{T} + 2B^{T} + 3C^{T}\) - the coefficient of \(C\) disagrees across the equals sign (2 on the left, 3 on the right), so the statement as printed is false. Verified in the intended form \((A + 2B + 3C)^{T} = A^{T} + 2B^{T} + 3C^{T}\) (the printed \(2C\) on the left looks like a repeat of the \(2\) in \(2B\)). The underlying property \((kA + lB + mC)^{T} = kA^{T} + lB^{T} + mC^{T}\) holds for any scalars, so the verification works equally with 2 on both sides.

solution:
\(B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(A + B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(\left( A + B^{T} \right)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

Also \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -3 \\ 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(A^{T} + B = \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -3 \\ 2 & 2 \\ 1 & -3 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(\therefore \left( A + B^{T} \right)^{T} = A^{T} + B\)

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 2 & 2 & -3 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(A + A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 2 \\ 5 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & -2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\). Interchanging its rows and columns reproduces the same matrix, so \(\left( A + A^{T} \right)^{T} = A + A^{T}\) and \(A + A^{T}\) is symmetric.

\(A - A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 0 & 4 \\ -6 & -4 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\). Its transpose is \(\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & -6 \\ -1 & 0 & -4 \\ 6 & 4 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = -\left( A - A^{T} \right)\), so \(A - A^{T}\) is skew symmetric.

Hence \(A + A^{T}\) is symmetric and \(A - A^{T}\) is skew symmetric.

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 3 & 4 \\ 2 & -7 & -5 \\ -4 & 2 & -3 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(A + A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & 5 & 0 \\ 5 & -14 & -3 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 \end{bmatrix}\). Interchanging its rows and columns reproduces the same matrix, so \(\left( A + A^{T} \right)^{T} = A + A^{T}\) and \(A + A^{T}\) is symmetric.

\(A - A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & -8 \\ 1 & 0 & 7 \\ 8 & -7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\). Its transpose is \(\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 1 & 8 \\ -1 & 0 & -7 \\ -8 & 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix} = -\left( A - A^{T} \right)\), so \(A - A^{T}\) is skew symmetric.

Hence \(A + A^{T}\) is symmetric and \(A - A^{T}\) is skew symmetric.

Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\). Then \(A = \frac{1}{2}\left( A + A^{T} \right) + \frac{1}{2}\left( A - A^{T} \right)\), where the first bracket is symmetric and the second skew symmetric.

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 3 \\ -2 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(A + A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 8 & 1 \\ 1 & -10 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A - A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -5 \\ 5 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2} & -5 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -\frac{5}{2} \\ \frac{5}{2} & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

Let \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 3 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 & 1 \\ -4 & -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\). Then \(A = \frac{1}{2}\left( A + A^{T} \right) + \frac{1}{2}\left( A - A^{T} \right)\), where the first bracket is symmetric and the second skew symmetric.

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 3 & -2 & -5 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}\), so \(A + A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 1 & -5 \\ 1 & -4 & -4 \\ -5 & -4 & 4 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A - A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 5 & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & 6 \\ -3 & -6 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\).

\(\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 3 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 & 1 \\ -4 & -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 6 & 1 & -5 \\ 1 & -4 & -4 \\ -5 & -4 & 4 \end{bmatrix} + \frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 5 & 3 \\ -5 & 0 & 6 \\ -3 & -6 & 0 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(A\) is \(3 \times 2\) and \(B\) is \(2 \times 3\), so \(AB\) is \(3 \times 3\).

\(AB = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & 7 & -9 \\ -4 & 11 & -14 \\ 2 & 11 & -15 \end{bmatrix}\)

\((AB)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 7 & 11 & 11 \\ -9 & -14 & -15 \end{bmatrix}\)

Also \(B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(B^{T}A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 7 & 11 & 11 \\ -9 & -14 & -15 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(\therefore (AB)^{T} = B^{T}A^{T}\)

\(B\) is \(2 \times 3\) and \(A\) is \(3 \times 2\), so \(BA\) is \(2 \times 2\).

\(BA = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 3 & -4 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -7 & -10 \\ 5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)

\((BA)^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -7 & 5 \\ -10 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)

Also \(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\) and \(B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), so

\(A^{T}B^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} -7 & 5 \\ -10 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)

\(\therefore (BA)^{T} = A^{T}B^{T}\)

\(A^{T} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\alpha & -\sin\alpha \\ \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \end{bmatrix}\)

\(A^{T}A = \begin{bmatrix} \cos\alpha & -\sin\alpha \\ \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} \cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \\ -\sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos^{2}\alpha + \sin^{2}\alpha & \cos\alpha\sin\alpha - \sin\alpha\cos\alpha \\ \sin\alpha\cos\alpha - \cos\alpha\sin\alpha & \sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha \end{bmatrix}\)

Using \(\sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1\), the diagonal entries are \(1\) and the off-diagonal entries are \(0\).

\(A^{T}A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I\)
